messages:
Preeta Rao: Quick follow-up on the auth consolidation RFC — we hit a couple of weird flows in staging today, want to sync before we push the next patch.
Mike Chen: OK — what surfaced?
Preeta Rao: Two things: 1) legacy project-scoped API keys still work when a service uses the operator proxy; 2) background jobs sometimes lose the original actor and show up as org-level calls.
Anna Latham: Can you paste a minimal repro for the job case?
Preeta Rao: Sure — job runner calls /v1/infer with header Authorization: ApiKey legacy-PRJ-abc, the proxy replaces actor with operator@infra when it retries. Observed in logs: `[job-runner] actor=project:123 api_key=legacy-PRJ-abc -> [operator-proxy] actor=operator@infra`
Jordan Kim: Hmm. That's the proxy behavior we expected for long-running retries (to centralize retry permission), but it breaks audit/owner mapping.
Mike Chen: Tradeoff: keep retry actor as operator (simpler perms) vs preserve original actor and escalate scope for retries (more complex role checks). Which do we prefer?
Preeta Rao: For compliance customers we need original actor preserved if possible. Can we attach a immutable "origin_actor" claim in the token the proxy mints?
Anna Latham: That sounds reasonable. Implementation idea: proxy issues ephemeral token with claims: `iss=proxy, sub=operator@infra, origin=project:123, origin_api_key=legacy-PRJ-abc`. Services treat `origin` as the audited actor but `sub` as the effective service for permission checks.
Jordan Kim: Concern: origin_api_key leakage in logs/metrics. We should hash the key or only include key id. Also watch for downstream services that currently use `sub` for billing.
Mike Chen: Agreed — replace `origin_api_key` with `origin_key_id` (no raw key). Add HMAC snapshot for integrity if we need tamper proof: `origin_sig=HMAC(kms-signing-key, origin_key_id|timestamp)`.
Preeta Rao: Nice. That lets us 1) keep permission checks deterministic (sub/operator), 2) preserve audit mapping (origin+sig), 3) avoid leaking secrets.
AuthBot: deploy:auth-proxy v2 rolled to staging at 2026-03-21T15:12:03Z :white_check_mark:
Anna Latham: Next edge: API key scoping semantics. If we unify namespaces (org vs project) we should make intent explicit on creation. Some customers rely on silent fallback: project key -> org key. That's messy.
Jordan Kim: Proposal: explicit creation flag `scope=project|org|global`. Add runtime rule: reject requests where key scope doesn't match the requested resource unless `x-fallback-allowed: true` header is present (for internal clients only).
Mike Chen: Implementation notes: SDKs should default to `scope=project` to be safe. Console UI warns about `global` keys.
Preeta Rao: Also need migration path for legacy keys. Plan: 1) auto-label legacy keys with inferred scope in metadata; 2) enable a warning-only mode for 2 weeks; 3) flip enforcement.
Anna Latham: Sounds good. Action items: (1) Mike to add origin_key_id + origin_sig to proxy token spec (PR), (2) Jordan to draft header-based fallback rule and SDK default, (3) Preeta to run a small staging migration to label legacy keys and surface warnings.
Mike Chen: I'll open the PR today, will include example token JSON and a small validator snippet.
Preeta Rao: Example validator snippet for services (psuedo):
```
if token.sub == 'operator@infra' and token.origin:
  audit_actor = token.origin
  effective_actor = token.sub
else:
  audit_actor = token.sub
  effective_actor = token.sub
```
Anna Latham: Minor QA note: check metrics pipelines for actor-based aggregation, we may need to switch to `audit_actor` for some dashboards.
Jordan Kim: +1. Also ensure rate-limits are charged to effective_actor (operator) not origin_actor to avoid owner confusion.
Preeta Rao: Thanks team — will sync after PRs land. :wave:
Mike Chen: thx, will link PR here when ready.
AuthBot: ci:pr/5634 passed all checks :rocket:
